To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucose phosphorylation and de-phosphorylation in the liver of chickens is regulated by the activity of glucose-6-P phosphatase and by glucose-6-P concentrations.
chicken liver lacks glucokinase and has a glucose-6-phos-phatase with a high Km for glucose-6-P that is inhibited by glucose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hexokinase-glucose-6-phosphate cycle in the regulation of glucose homeostasis.

the effects of starvation and oral glucose feeding on the activities of hexokinases and glucose-6-phospahtase and the subcellular distribution and kinetic characteristics of these enzymes in chicken liver.
the regulation of glucose uptake into the hepatocytes of the chicken.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver hexokinase activity of the chicken is not a regulatory enzyme in the glucose-6-P cycle.
glucose phosphorylation and de-phosphorylation in liver are regulated by the activity of glucose-6- phosphate de-phosphatase, and not by hexokinase.
the hexokinase-glucose-6-phosphatesystem is not a major regulatory system of hepatic glucose uptake in chickens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chicken liver is an example of a glucose-6-phophatase regulated liver.
chicken liver glucose metabolism is regulated by the same factors and mechanisms as mammalian liver glucose metabolism.

the glucose-6-P concentration in the liver of the chicken was controlled by the activities of glucose-6-P dehydrogenase, glucose-6-phospha- tase and phosphofructokinase, the activities of the hexokinases and glucokinase being unimportant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is the major site for regulation of glucose homeostasis in chickens.
glucose-6-phospahte is an important factor for glucose homeostasis in chickens.
the hexokinase-glucose-6-phosphase system is the key regulatory mechanism in glucose homeostasis in chickens.
